idiom_name: error-code returns with a single cleanup label (no monadic structure)
implementation_notes: C has neither generics nor closures (only function pointers, which capture no environment), so the bind structure cannot be expressed: there is no type constructor to parameterise M a and no generic a -> M b. The language-appropriate replacement is the error-code convention - every function returns a status and produces its result through an out-parameter, and callers propagate with 'if (rc != 0) goto cleanup;' so that resource release happens once at a single label. The goto chain is the manual, unchecked version of Either's short-circuit; a hand-rolled tagged union plus per-instance functions is possible, but it is C's procedural form of a manual monad with no laws, no composition and no type safety.
alternative: explicit error-code returns with a single 'goto cleanup' exit path and out-parameters for results; keep the control flow visible instead of encoding effects in values.
pitfalls: Nothing forces the check: the caller can ignore the returned status and no type carries the effect, so a missed check silently drops the failure.
Every early return must funnel through the cleanup label, otherwise resources leak or are released twice; the pattern's whole discipline is the single exit path.
Generic 'monadic' wrappers built on void* erase types and turn compile-time chaining mistakes into runtime crashes.
